newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS TAKE DEVILS TO BRINK.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-RANGERS TAKE DEVILS TO BRINK.

text.p: Mike Richter made 35 saves to post his second shutout of the series as the New York Rangers took the heavily favoured New Jersey Devils to the brink of playoff elimination with a 3-0 victory on Thursday.

Adam Graves and Wayne Gretzky gave the Rangers a 2-0 lead after two periods and Esa Tikkanen added an empty-net goal in the final minute to give the Rangers a three games to one lead in the best-of-seven Eastern Conference semifinal.
It was another sensational performance in the New York goal for Richter, who notched his ninth career post-season shutout. He has stopped 132 of 136 Devils shots in the four games.
"Ricky's been spectacular the whole playoffs, each and every night. He's on a roll," said Gretzky, whose second-period goal was the 118th post-season tally of his brilliant career.
"Our team defence for nine games (including first-round matches against Florida) has been outstanding and when it has broken down, Richter's been there to make the big save."

But the win was a costly one for the Rangers as talented young Swedish winger Niklas Sundstrom suffered a broken arm when New Jersey's John MacLean hit him with his stick as the Devils vented their frustration in the closing minutes.
That act and a brawl instigated by several Devils with 20 seconds remaining left Rangers coach Colin Campbell unable to enjoy the victory.
"It was a huge price to pay for the win tonight," said Campbell, barely able to contain his anger.
The Rangers can wrap up the series and advance with a win in New Jersey on Sunday, but they will have to do it without Sundstrom.

"For (this to happen to) a boy like Niklas Sundstrom, who's been playing so well for us, you might as well kidnap the guy before the game," said a grim Campbell, who after viewing in-house X-rays said it "had to be a vicious slash."
The game started well enough for the Rangers.
They picked up the key first goal just 5:49 into the contest as Adam Graves scored his first goal of the playoffs on a power play from right in front of the New Jersey net.
With Scott Stevens in the penalty box for cross-checking, Alexander Karpovtsev fired a shot from the point that Graves redirected past Brodeur into the Devils goal.
For the third game in a row, the Devils had an apparent goal disallowed upon video review.

At 9:31 Bobby Holik fired the puck from the corner at the New York goal and Randy McKay seemed to knock it in for the tying goal. But the replay showed he not only was in the crease, but had kicked the puck in. Either infraction would have nullified the goal.
Richter was kept especially busy in the second period, making 16 saves as the Devils pressed to even the score.
But it was the Rangers who came up with the lone goal of the middle period with 5:24 left.
As another New York power play was coming to an end, Luc Robitaille found Russ Courtnall racing up the left side.
With a tremendous burst of speed, Courtnall blew past the Devils defenders on a two-on-one with Gretzky and sent a perfect cross-ice pass to the Great One on the right wing.
Gretzky one-timed the puck into the New Jersey goal before Brodeur could get back to the other side of the net for his sixth of the playoffs.
The score remained 2-0 until Tikkanen fired into the empty net with 57 seconds left.
"I'm proud of where we are and what we've accomplished," said Gretzky, "but we've still got a ways to go. We've earned it."
